title: Engineered Lung Tissues Prepared from Decellularized Lung Slices
protocol: Use a laser cutter to cut tissue culture cassette frames and clips out of 3/32 inch thick polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) according to provided designs.
Cut tissue culture cassette tabs out of 1/16 inch thick PTFE using a laser cutter.
Soak seeding bath molds in a solution of 10% poloxamer 407 in distilled water overnight before use.
Fit the ring over the base of the mold and wrap in flexible plastic film to prevent leaking.
Mix PDMS elastomer with curing agent in a 10:1 ratio, pour into the 3D printed mold.
Degas the PDMS in a vacuum desiccator for 30 min to remove air bubbles.
Bake seeding baths at 60 °C for 8 h.
Prepare a split perfusion system comprising gravity- and pump-driven limbs.
Connect a pulmonary artery (PA) cannula to the end of the tubing as specified.
Prime the lines with PBS containing 100 U/mL heparin and 0.01 mg/mL sodium nitroprusside (SNP).
Pre-set the perfusion pump to 30 mL/min.
Dose an adult Sprague-Dawley rat with an intraperitoneal injection of 400 U/kg heparin for anti-coagulation.
Inject ketamine (75 mg/kg) and xylazine (5 mg/kg) IP for anesthesia.
Confirm a surgical plane of anesthesia via lack of response to noxious stimulus.
Trim the chest and abdomen of fur using hair clippers.
Spray with 70% ethanol and wipe three times with 10% povidone-iodine.
Grasp the skin below the level of the diaphragm with rat tooth forceps.
Make a half-inch transverse incision in the skin with fine-pointed scissors.
Grasp the exposed abdominal fascia with the forceps.
Make a half-inch transverse incision in the fascia and extend it through the skin and fascia across the width of the upper abdomen.
Use the tip of the fine scissors to make a small incision in the center of the anterior diaphragm.
Extend the incision across the full width of the chest.
Make two vertical incisions through the full height of the ribcage toward the neck.
Extend the incision through the left ribs to cut through the collarbone and along the side of the neck to the level of the larynx, exposing the trachea.
Dissect the trachea free from surrounding connective tissue and from the esophagus.
Make a transverse incision across the anterior half of the trachea between two cartilage rings, close to the larynx.
Thread a 4-0 polypropylene suture behind the trachea, below the level of the incision.
Loosely pre-tie the first half of a surgeon's knot with two twists using the suture.

Place a cannula comprising a 1/16 inch barbed Y-connecter connected to a one-way check valve and a ½ inch length of LS 14 silicone tubing into the trachea by inserting one limb of the Y-connector into the tracheal incision toward the direction of the lungs.
Position the pre-tied suture loop around the trachea at the level of the inserted cannula.
Tighten the suture around the inserted Y-connector to secure the cannula in place.
Add two single-twist throws of the suture to complete the knot.
Fill a 10 mL syringe with air and connect it to the luer-lock of the tracheal cannula.
Clamp the inferior vena cava close to the diaphragm using a curved hemostat.
Inject the heart with 150 U heparin via the right ventricle (RV).
Partially open the gravity line stopcock to produce a slow but steady dripping of PBS/heparin/SNP from the PA cannula.
Thread the needle of a 4-0 polypropylene suture behind the base of the pulmonary artery (PA) where it exits the RV.
Pre-tie a loose loop of suture around the base of the PA using the first half of a surgeon's knot.
Make a small incision in the RV just below and perpendicular to the PA using fine scissors.
Insert one limb of the PA cannula Y-connector into the base of the PA.
Secure the suture around the PA and the inserted connector and complete the surgeon's knot with an additional single-twist throw.
Attach a one-way valve to the other end of the PA catheter Y-connector.
Cut off the apex of the heart to allow blood flow efflux via the left ventricle.
Switch the perfusion line to the pump side using the stopcock connecting the two lines.
Turn on the pump at 30 mL/min.
Manually ventilate the lungs via the 10 mL tracheal syringe at approximately 10-15 breaths/min while perfusing the lungs via the PA.
Perfuse the lungs until they turn mostly white, usually requiring 40 mL of PBS/heparin/SNP or less.
Cut the posterior trachea just above the level of the tracheal cannula.
Dissect the lungs and heart free of all remaining connective tissue.
Extract the lungs and heart en bloc.
Fill a 10 mL syringe with 2% low melting point agarose in Hank's balanced salt solution (HBSS) without phenol red, prewarmed to 42 °C.
Manually inflate the extracted lungs 3x with 10 mL of air via the trachea cannula.
Immediately inject the prepared syringe of agarose via the trachea cannula at a rate of approximately 40 mL/min until the most distal tips of the lung lobes are inflated.
Inject an additional 1-2 mL of agarose if distal regions of lung remain collapsed.
Cap the trachea by attaching the white cap from a 4-way stopcock to the female luer-lock of the tracheal cannula.
Place the lung in a 150 mm Petri dish on ice to allow the agarose to solidify.
Inflate the lung shortly after extraction to ensure uniform filling of the lung parenchyma.
Pre-chill the metal chilling block at -20 °C and keep it on ice when not using throughout the slicing procedure.
Attach a blade to the blade holder with a small drop of cyanoacrylate glue.
Carefully attach the blade holder to the vibratome using an Allen wrench so that it just lines up with the end of a specimen tube inserted into the buffer tray.
Prepare 6-well plates with 3 mL per well sterile ice-cold HBSS without phenol red to collect the slices.
Using a scalpel, cut a piece of lung tissue approximately 1-1.5 cm³.
Place a small drop of cyanoacrylate glue onto the plunger of the specimen tube.
Dab lung tissue on a paper wipe to remove excess moisture, and then immediately place the lung tissue on top of the plunger using forceps.
Slide the metal tube up to the level of the top of the tissue with the plunger receded.
Pipette pre-warmed 2% agarose in HBSS into the top of the tube to surround the tissue.
Place the ice-cold chilling block around the tissue for about 1 min to allow the agarose to solidify.
Insert the specimen tube into the buffer tray.
Fill the tray with ice-cold PBS to mid-way up the tissue block.
Turn the motor box switch to fast forward (FF) to advance the plunger so it touches the base of the specimen tube.
Set the desired slice thickness, cutting speed, and oscillation frequency.
Select Continuous mode and flip the switch to On to begin slicing.
Transfer tissue slices into a buffer tray using an inoculating loop or spatula.
Stop slicing when approximately 2 mm of tissue remains in the specimen tube.
Repeat steps to slice additional lung tissue as needed.
Decellularize slices immediately for scaffold preparation, or snap-freeze and store at -80 °C for up to 2 months.
Transfer 4-6 slices to a 35 mm Petri dish.
Aspirate excess fluid from around the slices carefully.
Place dishes in a bath of dry ice and 100% ethanol to snap-freeze.
Wrap dishes in foil, seal in a plastic bag, and transfer to -80 °C freezer.
Fill a 100 mm Petri dish about one-third full with PBS.
Transfer cassettes and tabs to the dish using forceps.
Thaw one dish at a time by pouring room temperature PBS into the dish to cover the slices if using frozen slices.
Transfer a thawed slice to a 150 mm Petri dish.
Gently unfold the slice using fine forceps, if necessary.
Aspirate excess PBS from around the tissue.
Cut a 3 mm wide strip from the slice using a razor blade with a ruler as a guide or an alternative rotary cutter with custom-made spacer.
Avoid any tears, holes, large airways or vessels, thick connective tissue.
Transfer the tissue strip to the prepared 100 mm Petri dish using forceps.
Clip the tissue strip into the cassette by floating it above the cassette and centering it to overhang the holes at either end.
With fine forceps, place a tab partly into the hole at one end of the cassette.
Gently straighten the tissue and then place the second tab.
Using forceps in each hand, press each tab in completely to secure the tissue.
If having difficulty keeping the tissue in place prior to clipping, aspirate some PBS from the dish to lower the fluid level.

Begin step 1 of the decellularization protocol: using a curved hemostat to grasp the notched sides of each cassette, transfer cassettes to 6-well plates filled with 3 mL of PBS + ions + antibiotics/antimycotics per well.
Place well plates on an orbital shaker at 30 rpm for 10 min.
Aspirate the fluid from each well and replace it with 3 mL/well PBS + ions.
Place the plate back on the orbital shaker at 30 rpm and incubate for 5 min.
Repeat steps 3.3.4 for each of the solutions and corresponding durations as outlined in the decellularization protocol.
Transfer tissues to sterile 6-well plates with fresh PBS + antibiotics/antimycotics after the final rinse step with PBS + antibiotics/antimycotics (step 20 of Table 2).
Incubate at 37 °C for 48 h.
If using tissue scaffolds stored at 4 °C, incubate scaffolds overnight at 37 °C with fresh PBS + antibiotics/antimycotics prior to seeding.
Rinse scaffolds 3x with sterile PBS (5 mL/well), 5 min each.
Examine scaffolds under a phase contrast microscope at 5x magnification to select tissues for seeding.
Count endothelial cells using a hemocytometer.
Prepare the endothelial cell suspension in endothelial medium at 5 x 10^6 cells/mL, sufficient for seeding 500,000 endothelial cells per slice.
Place autoclaved seeding baths in 100 mm Petri dishes.
Transfer rinsed scaffolds upside down to seeding baths using a fine curved hemostat and straight hemostat or forceps.

Grasp the cassette by the notched sides with the fine curved hemostat, grasp one end of the cassette carefully with the straight hemostat or forceps without touching the tissue, and place in a seeding bath well.
Ensure scaffolds are centered upside down in the bottom of each well.
Press gently on the corner of the cassette if necessary to ensure it is seated flat in the well.
Swirl the prepared cell suspension gently to mix.
Pipette 100 μL cells directly on top of each tissue at the base of the well.
Transfer seeded tissues to the cell culture incubator at 37 °C/5% CO2.
Add 900 µL pre-warmed culture medium to each well using a manual pipette after 2 h.
Gently press down on the corner of the cassette with the pipette tip if it floats upon adding medium.
Change medium on day -2 by tilting the Petri dish and manually pipetting out the medium.
Replace with 1 mL of fresh endothelial medium per well.
Count AEC2s and fibroblasts using a hemocytometer.
Prepare a 1:1 cell suspension of AEC2s and fibroblasts in AEC2 growth medium at 5 x 10^6 total cells/mL.
Pipette out the medium from each well of the seeding bath.
Swirl the prepared cell suspension gently to mix.
Pipette 100 µL cells directly on top of each tissue at the base of the well.
Transfer seeded tissues to the cell culture incubator at 37 °C/5% CO2.
Add 900 µL pre-warmed AEC2 growth medium to each well after 2 h of seeding.
Prepare a 12-well plate with 1 mL of pre-warmed AEC2 growth medium per well per cassette on day 1.
Pipette 800 µL of medium from each well of the seeding bath.
Remove cassettes from the seeding bath using a fine curved hemostat via the holes along the notched sides.
Transfer each cassette to a straight hemostat or forceps at one end, then flip and transfer right-side-up to the prepared 12-well plate.
Change culture medium in the 12-well plate every other day until day 7 using a glass Pasteur pipette.
Transfer tissue culture cassettes to 10% neutral-buffered formalin.
Incubate the tissues in formalin for 3-4 hours at room temperature on a rocker.
Cut tissues from cassettes using the tip of a fine-pointed forceps where they meet the tabs.
Process tissues according to routine methods for paraffin embedding and histology.
Rinse tissues in cassettes with PBS twice.
Remove tissues from cassettes for snap freezing or proceed with lysis for RNA extraction.
